```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Dependencies and datasets: docs/COLLEAGUE_RUN_GUIDE.md and docs/SCRIPT_REFERENCE.md.
# Matching R entry orchestrates input preparation and models; this template renders its results.
# Restore packages once with Rscript R/install_dependencies.R; inputs are runtime parameters.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE)
stopifnot(nzchar(params$prepared_dir))
emit<-function(...)cat(...,sep="")
work<-params$prepared_dir
x<-readRDS(file.path(work,"score_profile_examples.rds"))
esc<-function(v){v<-gsub("&","&amp;",as.character(v),fixed=TRUE);v<-gsub("<","&lt;",v,fixed=TRUE);gsub(">","&gt;",v,fixed=TRUE)}
f<-function(v,d=1)sprintf(paste0("%.",d,"f"),v)
score<-function(v)sprintf("%+.3f",v)
pct<-function(v)paste0(f(v),"%")
N<-function(v)format(v,big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE,trim=TRUE)
table_html<-function(headers,rows){paste0('<div class="table-wrap"><table><thead><tr><th>',paste(headers,collapse="</th><th>"),'</th></tr></thead><tbody>',paste(vapply(rows,function(r)paste0('<tr><td>',paste(r,collapse='</td><td>'),'</td></tr>'),character(1)),collapse=""),'</tbody></table></div>')}
figure<-function(name){p<-file.path(work,name);s<-readChar(p,file.info(p)$size,useBytes=TRUE);paste0('<figure><img alt="Component contributions to the two area scores" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,',jsonlite::base64_enc(charToRaw(s)),'"></figure>')}
value<-function(q,geo,k)q$components$raw_pct[q$components$geo==geo&q$components$variable==k]
label<-function(k)esc(unname(x$labels[k]))
summary_rows<-lapply(x$selected,function(q){a<-q$a;b<-q$b
 contrast<-if(q$case$case_id=="lagos_supply")"Similar totals conceal different service weaknesses: training in Ikorodu versus offering and LARC stock in Ibeju-Lekki."else paste0(a$area,": ",a$unfavorable_components,"/6 components above-average challenges; ",b$area,": ",b$unfavorable_components,"/6. ",f(100*b$largest_positive_share),"% of ",b$area,"’s positive component points come from ",label(b$largest_positive_component),".")
 c(paste0('<b>',esc(a$country_label),'</b><br>',a$side),paste0(esc(a$area),' <b>',score(a$score),'</b><br>',esc(b$area),' <b>',score(b$score),'</b>'),f(q$score_gap,3),contrast)
})
```

</style>')
emit('<header><span class="eyebrow">SURGO × UNIVERSITY OF MANITOBA · SCORE INTERPRETATION</span><h1>Similar total scores can describe very different challenges</h1><p>Real examples from the updated Lagos, Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire Rural/Urban reports. Averages summarize the level of concern or service weakness, but can conceal which components are elevated and which favorable components offset them.</p><nav><a href="#overview">Overview</a><a href="#lagos">Lagos</a><a href="#senegal">Senegal</a><a href="#cotedivoire">Côte d’Ivoire</a><a href="#methods">Methods and caveats</a></nav></header><main>')
emit('<section id="overview"><span class="eyebrow">READ THE TOTAL WITH ITS COMPONENTS</span><h2>Six examples with totals within 0.10 index points</h2><p class="scope"><b>Scope:</b> these are the <b>administrative-area planning scores</b> in the Rural/Urban reports. Supply pools Rural and Urban FP facilities within each area. They are not the residence-specific supply exposures or personal demand scores used in the woman-level models.</p><p>Both sides are displayed as <b>higher = more challenges</b>. Both report scores use the same direction: higher values indicate more measured constraints. No classifications or underlying working reports have been changed. A positive total means above-average challenges relative to the stated country’s surveyed-area references; it is not an absolute severity threshold.</p><div class="summary">',table_html(c('Geography / side','Areas and total scores','Absolute difference','What the total conceals'),summary_rows),'</div><p class="note">“Above-average” uses the equal-area reference means used for standardization, not the survey-weighted overall country percentage. Examples are selected illustrations, not an exhaustive or statistically representative sample of areas. Some totals are only moderately above zero.</p></section>')
for(country in c("lagos","senegal","cotedivoire")){
 title<-c(lagos="Lagos",senegal="Senegal",cotedivoire="Côte d’Ivoire")[[country]]
 emit('<section id="',country,'"><span class="eyebrow">PAIRED AREA PROFILES</span><h2>',title,'</h2>')
 for(side in c("Demand","Supply")){
  q<-x$selected[[paste(country,tolower(side),sep="_")]];a<-q$a;b<-q$b;id<-q$case$case_id
  emit('<article class="case ',tolower(side),'"><h3>',side,': ',esc(a$area),' and ',esc(b$area),'</h3>')
  if(id=="lagos_demand"){
   takeaway<-paste0('Ifako-Ijaye has five above-average concern components; Apapa has four, with opposition to FP contributing ',f(100*b$largest_positive_share),'% of its positive component points. Permission barriers are ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'agency')),' in Ifako-Ijaye versus ',pct(value(q,b$geo,'agency')),' in Apapa, while opposition is ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'opposes')),' versus ',pct(value(q,b$geo,'opposes')),'. This is a moderate difference in concentration, not an all-six-versus-one example.')
   planning<-'A similar overall concern score does not call for an identical response. Review permission/agency circumstances in Ifako-Ijaye and FP opposition in Apapa alongside their other concerns; these comparisons do not estimate intervention effects.'
  }else if(id=="lagos_supply"){
   takeaway<-paste0('Ikorodu’s clearest standardized weakness is trained-provider share (',pct(value(q,a$geo,'training')),'). Ibeju-Lekki instead has much lower short/long-acting offering and LARC-stock indicators (both ',pct(value(q,b$geo,'offering')),'). Ibeju-Lekki’s stronger free provision (',pct(value(q,b$geo,'free')),') and training (',pct(value(q,b$geo,'training')),') offset its availability weaknesses mathematically. Similar totals conceal different service problems, rather than a pure broad-versus-single-component contrast.')
   planning<-'Review training and free-product coverage in Ikorodu; investigate the offering/stock pattern in Ibeju-Lekki. A favorable training or free-provision value cannot literally substitute for an unavailable method.'
  }else if(id=="senegal_demand"){
   takeaway<-paste0('Bignona’s confidence indicator is ',pct(value(q,b$geo,'confidence')),' versus ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'confidence')),' in Mbacké, and supplies ',f(100*b$largest_positive_share),'% of Bignona’s positive component points. Mbacké has four above-average components, including health beliefs (',pct(value(q,a$geo,'health')),') and opposition (',pct(value(q,a$geo,'opposes')),'). Its confidence component is only slightly above its reference mean. The total scores differ by just ',f(q$score_gap,3),'.')
   planning<-'Bignona warrants closer examination of confidence choosing or managing a method; Mbacké shows a broader mix of concerns. The confidence item is not an objective knowledge test, so its label should not be interpreted as proof of factual ignorance.'
  }else if(id=="senegal_supply"){
   takeaway<-paste0('Matam’s daily-provision ratio is ',pct(value(q,b$geo,'daily_provision')),' versus ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'daily_provision')),' in Goudiry, against a reference area mean of ',pct(q$components$reference_raw_mean[q$components$geo==b$geo&q$components$variable=='daily_provision']),'. Daily provision supplies ',f(100*b$largest_positive_share),'% of Matam’s positive component points; its other two unfavorable components are barely above zero. Goudiry combines lower method offering (',pct(value(q,a$geo,'offering')),') with limited daily provision and two smaller weaknesses.')
   planning<-'Investigate regularity of reported method provision in Matam; Goudiry’s profile also calls for examining the method range. Supply evidence uses facility records, not the number of surveyed women in these départements.'
  }else if(id=="cotedivoire_demand"){
   takeaway<-paste0('Yamoussoukro’s confidence indicator is ',pct(value(q,b$geo,'confidence')),' versus ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'confidence')),' in Divo and supplies ',f(100*b$largest_positive_share),'% of its positive component points. Divo has five above-average components; permission barriers are ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'agency')),' versus ',pct(value(q,b$geo,'agency')),' and opposition is ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'opposes')),' versus ',pct(value(q,b$geo,'opposes')),'.')
   planning<-'Review Divo’s broader agency, fertility-belief and FP-opposition profile. Yamoussoukro’s confidence, health and fertility concerns suggest a different emphasis for further service and communication assessment.'
  }else{
   takeaway<-paste0('Gagnoa’s free-product proportion is ',pct(value(q,b$geo,'free')),' and supplies ',f(100*b$largest_positive_share),'% of its positive component points. Koun-Fao has more distributed weaknesses: offering ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'offering')),', free-product provision ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'free')),' and LARC stock ',pct(value(q,a$geo,'larc_stock')),'. Its stronger daily provision and training offset part of those weaknesses, giving a similar total.')
   planning<-'Investigate recorded free provision in Gagnoa; in Koun-Fao examine the combination of method offering, LARC stock and free provision. These are facility-average product measures, not the percentage of women receiving free care.'
  }
  emit('<div class="metrics">')
  for(v in list(a,b))emit('<div class="metric"><b>',esc(v$area),' · ',score(v$score),'</b><span>',v$unfavorable_components,'/6 components above-average challenges · largest component supplies ',f(100*v$largest_positive_share),'% of positive component points</span><small>',if(side=='Demand')paste0(N(v$n_need),' women in need; valid domain Ns ',N(v$min_valid),'–',N(v$max_valid))else paste0(N(v$fp_facilities),' FP facilities; valid measure Ns ',N(v$min_valid),'–',N(v$max_valid)),'</small></div>')
  emit('</div>',figure(q$svg),'<div class="callout"><b>What the total conceals.</b> ',takeaway,'<br><b>Planning interpretation.</b> ',planning,'</div>')
  ca<-q$components[q$components$geo==a$geo,];cb<-q$components[q$components$geo==b$geo,];cb<-cb[match(ca$variable,cb$variable),]
  rows<-lapply(seq_len(nrow(ca)),function(j)c(esc(ca$label[j]),paste0(pct(ca$raw_pct[j]),' <small>(valid n=',N(ca$n_valid[j]),')</small>'),paste0(pct(cb$raw_pct[j]),' <small>(valid n=',N(cb$n_valid[j]),')</small>'),pct(ca$reference_raw_mean[j]),score(ca$risk_z[j]),score(cb$risk_z[j])))
  emit('<details><summary>Underlying percentages, valid denominators and component z-scores</summary>',table_html(c('Component',esc(a$area),esc(b$area),'Reference area mean','Area A challenge z','Area B challenge z'),rows),'<p class="note">Demand raw percentages: higher = more reported concern. Supply raw percentages: higher = more favorable except stockout burden. All displayed challenge z-scores are aligned higher = worse. The reference mean is computed across the same areas used by the source report, giving each area equal weight. These component z-scores sum to six times the total score.</p></details></article>')
 }
 if(country=="lagos"){
  aa<-x$profiles[x$profiles$country=='lagos'&x$profiles$side=='Supply'&x$profiles$geo=='AJEROMIIFELODUN',];bb<-x$profiles[x$profiles$country=='lagos'&x$profiles$side=='Supply'&x$profiles$geo=='OJO',]
  emit('<details><summary>Additional Lagos supply example: broader versus fewer weaknesses</summary><p>Ajeromi-Ifelodun has supply challenge ',score(aa$score),' with all six components unfavorable relative to the Lagos references. Ojo has ',score(bb$score),' with four unfavorable components, daily provision being the largest. This supports the breadth distinction, although Ojo is not a single-component-dominated case: its largest component is ',f(100*bb$largest_positive_share),'% of its positive component points.</p></details>')
 }
 emit('</section>')
}
emit('<section id="methods"><span class="eyebrow">CONSTRUCTION, SELECTION AND LIMITS</span><h2>Interpretation of these examples</h2><p class="rule">Total challenge score = (z₁ + z₂ + z₃ + z₄ + z₅ + z₆) / 6</p><p>The same total can come from six moderately positive terms or a large positive term offset by negative terms. Positive component points are summed separately only to describe concentration. Their largest-component share is <b>max(positive z) / sum(positive z)</b>; it is not a percentage of nonuse, a percentage explained by a model, or a percentage of the net total. Counting all positive z-values also counts barely positive values, so consult the plotted magnitudes.</p><p>The search considered complete area profiles with positive totals on both sides of a pair and an absolute total-score difference no larger than 0.10 original average-z points. The selected illustrations have at least 50 valid women per demand domain or 20 valid FP facilities per supply component. These are explicit exploratory selection rules, not validated severity or precision thresholds. We did not find an equally strong broad-versus-single-component example in every setting; the Lagos cases are qualified accordingly.</p><p>Demand percentages use survey weights among original SURGO FPN2 = 1 women with consent and positive weight, excluding unresolved answers per domain. Supply values average confirmed FP providers with valid data separately per measure; there are no facility weights. Supply challenge is negative favorable readiness, reversing stockout burden appropriately. In Côte d’Ivoire, the five supply-unassessed areas are excluded from complete supply profile comparisons.</p><p>The score sums were independently checked against the saved reports for all ',nrow(x$profiles),' complete area-side profiles, and source report-input hashes remained unchanged. These are point-estimate illustrations; no tests establish that the differences are statistically resolved. Indicators overlap and are not independent causes. The original geographic sampling, missingness and stock-coding limitations remain applicable.</p><div class="callout"><b>Component information beside the total score:</b> the total summarizes the overall profile. The six component percentages/contributions, number above average, largest component and valid Ns reveal its composition. Neither the total nor a top-three list establishes an intervention choice. Where only one component is substantially elevated, a list of three can make the evidence appear broader than it is.</div><p>The OECD/JRC handbook explains that arithmetic aggregation permits strengths in one component to offset weaknesses in another. This is a property to make explicit, not proof that the index calculation is wrong. <a href="https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2008/08/handbook-on-constructing-composite-indicators-methodology-and-user-guide_g1gh9301/9789264043466-en.pdf">OECD/JRC Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators, aggregation discussion</a>.</p></section></main><footer>Separate diagnostic of the updated Rural/Urban reports. The existing scores, classifications and model definitions are retained.</footer>')
emit('\n```\n')
